title: Colleagues
hookLine: faith at work mostly looks like honesty and kindness
tomorrow: a stranger at the counter needs time you don't have. now what?

lines: A MILK STEAMER, A JAMMED PRINTER.
cards: The hiss of a milk steamer. A printer jamming again. Keys clicking in an office before anyone's had coffee.
A workday is mostly noise, and almost none of it is about God. So what does faith at work sound like when nobody mentions God? Mostly, small honest sentences: that was my mistake.
I'll cover your shift. She did that, not me.

teach.b: In the Bible, faith at work looks less like a sermon by the coffee machine and more like Daniel's record.
His rivals went looking for something to accuse him of, and “they could find none occasion nor fault; forasmuch as he was faithful.”
Paul writes to the church at Thessalonica: “study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands,” so “that ye may walk honestly toward them that are without.”
Study to be quiet: make a project of being calm, minding your work, being the colleague people trust with the details.
Colossians says whose eyes the work is really for: “And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.”
And Ephesians puts honesty plainly: “putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another.” Members one of another, like parts of one body.
Here's one to repeat tonight: in Daniel's story, the only thing his rivals could think to use against him was the law of his God.
At work, quiet faith sounds like small truths: the deadline that will slip, the mistake that was yours, the credit that belongs to someone else.
Quiet doesn't mean silent when something's wrong. It means calm, honest and steady.

how: Day to day, Christians often live their faith at work without speaking of it: honest work, fair credit, kindness to coworkers; some say a short prayer before a shift or a hard meeting.

o: the people you work beside, who meet your faith in how you treat them
the members of a church who serve on a committee together
people in your line of work you only know online

games.q: faith at work, quietly — tap the pairs.
p: as to the Lord, not unto men

s: quiet faith at work means never speaking up
Ephesians: put away lying and speak truth. quiet means calm, not silent.
Daniel's rivals could find no fault in him except about his God's law
they could find none occasion nor fault, forasmuch as he was faithful.
Colossians says to work hard so the boss will notice
"as to the Lord, and not unto men."

games.q: your team lead praises you for a fix your coworker actually made. the meeting's moving on. what fits quietly faithful?
o: say nothing; it's not worth the awkward moment.
say plainly, "that was her fix," and move on.
take it, and give her credit some other time.
games.why: Ephesians: put away lying and speak truth with your neighbor, for we are members one of another. quiet faith sounds like small, plain truths.

practice: Rest your hands palms up and look at them: the cups, keys, tools or keyboards they handled this week. Rub them together slowly until they're warm, then lay them still.
If you pray, offer the next day's work through them; if not, just feel the warmth fade.

wordCard.voice: Colleagues. The people we work beside, who may never hear a word about faith and still meet it in how they're treated.

orig.note: Greek in Colossians 3:23, rendered heartily in the KJV.

carryVoice: Keep this one: quietly faithful, which is calm and honest, and never silent about the truth. Day seventeen-nineteen.
